newsitem.title: USA: US foreign crude demand seen, arbitrage seen tight.
newsitem.headline: US foreign crude demand seen, arbitrage seen tight.

text.p: U.S. refiners keeping pace with high refinery capacities were still seen sourcing foreign supplies, but mostly from within the region due to tight import arbitrage opportunities.
Light, sweet crudes appropriate for distillate production were offered into the Gulf, but at strong prices.
Qua Iboe was reported offered around Dated Brent plus $1.90 cents a barrel cif Gulf Coast, with Cusiana also seen available for Nov lifting at Dec WTI plus 15-25 cents fob.
Brent was barely talked on a delivered basis, but traded thrice on an fob basis at Nov Brent parity.
The cargoes were for Oct 24-26, 20-22 and 23-25 windows.
In the nearby Latin American markets, Argentine YPF sold 380,000 barrels of Escalante loading mid-Nov at around WTI minus $3.12 a barrel fob.
Another 380,000 barrel cargo was offered for Nov 23-24, traders said.
Elsewhere, Colombia's Ecopetrol was said to have sold three cargoes of South Blend to a European refiner taking the shipment to a Peruvian refinery, where they hold equity.
The cargo was rumored sold as high as a discount of $2.25 against WTI, and as low as minus $2.85.
In the U.S. after market, Dec Brent traded at $23.30 a barrel for a full cargo, down from the IPE close of $23.58, and down a total of 97 cents from Wednesday's close.
Brent intermonth Nov/Dec traded at plus 37 and 35 cents, slightly lower than the late London session.
